Aftercare

The first 7 to 10 days
matter most.

Your treatment team will give you personalised aftercare. These general principles help protect a new PMU result as it heals.

Keep it calm

Keep the area clean and dry. Gently dab—never rub—and use only the thin balm layer recommended for your treatment.

Pause the extras

Skip makeup, steam, saunas, swimming and heavy workouts while the treated area is healing.

Protect the pigment

Avoid direct sun and tanning. Once healed, use SPF daily to help preserve your colour.

Let it heal naturally

Do not pick, scratch or peel. Let any flakes release on their own for the most even healed finish.

Long term: avoid chemical peels, retinol, lasers and strong exfoliants directly over treated areas, and speak with your artist before planning any skin procedures.

Brow guide

Microblading, ombre
or combination brows?

The best technique is the one that fits your skin, brow goals and lifestyle—not the one currently trending.

Microblading

Fine hair-like strokes create a natural, feathery look. It can suit normal to dry skin and typically fades over 12 to 18 months.

Ombre brows

Tiny pigment dots make a soft, powdered gradient. It can suit oily skin and people who enjoy a more filled-in brow, usually fading over 18 to 36 months.

Combination brows

Hair strokes through the front with soft shading through the body and tail. It offers realism with additional depth for many skin types.

Not sure? A consultation lets us assess skin texture, natural hair growth and the level of definition that feels right for you.

Academy guide

How to begin a career
in permanent makeup.

PMU is creative and technical. The strongest start comes from safe training, supervised practice and a plan for professional standards.

  1. 01

    Check local requirements

    Licensing and registration vary by location. Confirm your local health authority or council requirements before training.

  2. 02

    Choose training carefully

    Look for small classes, anatomy and hygiene theory, supervised practice, and a clear assessment process.

  3. 03

    Build one specialism first

    Many artists begin with brows, then add lips, eyeliner or SMP after gaining confidence.

  4. 04

    Practise and keep learning

    Build a consented portfolio, arrange insurance and keep developing your technique and colour knowledge.
